test_title: PYST 25: SSC MTS 2024 - English Language and Comprehension (Held On: 18 Oct, 2024 - Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to replace the underlined segment.
He thinks his new plan will undoubtedly __produce the desired result__.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. **bear fruit**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"bear fruit"** means to produce successful results or yield the desired outcome. (फल देना)
 
 
• **Example:** Her hard work and perseverance finally bore fruit when she received the promotion.
 
 

 
• The given word **"desired result"** refers to the outcome or effect that someone hopes to achieve. (वांछित परिणाम)
 
 
• **Example:** The new marketing strategy is expected to bring the desired result for the company.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **bear fruit**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Go suck a lemon** (नींबू चूसने जाओ): A rude phrase used to dismiss someone or express irritation.
 
 
• **Example:** When he kept bothering her, she told him to go suck a lemon.
 

 
• **Sour grapes** (खट्टे अंगूर): Refers to a situation where someone pretends to dislike something they cannot have.
 
 
• **Example:** After failing to win the competition, he said it wasn't important anyway, which seemed like sour grapes.
 

 
• **Go pear-shaped** (बिगड़ जाना): Refers to a situation going wrong or failing unexpectedly.
 
 
• **Example:** The project went pear-shaped when the team missed the deadline.
